description: ICE Ready — Know Your Rights card. Reference only, not identification.

primaryFields.label: Know Your Rights
primaryFields.value: You do not have to answer.

secondaryFields.label: SAY THIS
secondaryFields.value: I am exercising my right to remain silent.

secondaryFields.label: SAY THIS
secondaryFields.value: I do not consent to a search.

backFields.label: This is not identification
backFields.value: This card is a reference. It is not issued by any government, it does not prove who you are, and it does not establish immigration status or citizenship. Carry your real documents and know where they are.

backFields.label: At the door
backFields.value: You do not have to open the door. Ask the officer to slide any warrant under the door. A warrant must be signed by a judge and must name your address. An ICE administrative form (I-200 or I-205) signed by an ICE officer is not a judicial warrant and does not authorize entry.

backFields.label: If you are stopped
backFields.value: Stay calm. Do not run. Do not lie and do not show false documents. You may say: I am exercising my right to remain silent. I want to speak to a lawyer. Do not sign anything you do not understand or that you have not shown to a lawyer.

backFields.label: Your phone
backFields.value: Turn off Face ID and fingerprint unlock and set a strong passcode. Courts have repeatedly allowed police to compel a face or a finger. A passcode is treated very differently.

backFields.label: For your family
backFields.value: Make sure someone else knows your A-number, your attorney's name and number, and where your documents are. A plan that only lives in your head does not survive a detention.

backFields.label: Get the app
backFields.value: ICE Ready is free, works offline, requires no account, and never uploads anything. iceready.app

backFields.label: Not legal advice
backFields.value: This card is general information, not legal advice, and does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws differ by state and change over time. Talk to an immigration attorney about your situation.
